globalProps.name: GlobalProps
globalProps.description: Global props available on all Playbook components for consistent spacing, layout, and styling.

responsiveUsage.description: Props marked responsive accept breakpoint objects.

domSafeProps.description: Use domSafeProps() to filter non-DOM props when spreading.

advanced_table.name: AdvancedTable
advanced_table.description: The Advanced Table can be used to display complex, nested data in a way that allows for expansion and/or sorting.

rails.example:
<%= pb_rails("advanced_table", props: {
  column_definitions: column_definitions,
  table_data: table_data
}) %>
rails.note: Define column_definitions / table_data in the view or helper using the same shapes as playgrounds/advanced_table.json samples.

avatar.name: Avatar
avatar.description: User photo for recognition. Prefer User when showing a name; Avatar alone if names are hidden.

rails.example: <%= pb_rails("avatar", props: { size: "md", name: "Jane Doe", image_url: "https://randomuser.me/api/portraits/women/44.jpg" }) %>

background.name: Background
background.description: The Background component is used for adding a background to a page or to any container.

rails.example:
<%= pb_rails("background", props: { background_color: "light", padding: "md" }) do %>
  Default light background
<% end %>

badge.name: Badge
badge.description: Badges can be used for notification, tags, and status. They are used for count and numbers.

rails.example: <%= pb_rails("badge", props: { variant: "primary", text: "Primary" }) %>

body.name: Body
body.description: Default paragraph style. Step to light, then lighter, only to de-emphasize supporting lines.

react.example:
<Body>
  This is standard body copy in a paragraph element, ideal for articles, forms, and long-form content.
</Body>

rails.example:
<%= pb_rails("body", props: {  }) do %>
  This is standard body copy in a paragraph element, ideal for articles, forms, and long-form content.
<% end %>

bread_crumbs.name: BreadCrumbs
bread_crumbs.description: BreadCrumbs can be used for keeping a user aware of their route location.

rails.example:
<%= pb_rails("bread_crumbs", props: {  }) do %>
  <BreadCrumbItem href="/">Home</BreadCrumbItem><BreadCrumbItem component="span">Settings</BreadCrumbItem>
<% end %>

button.name: Button
button.description: Primary Button for main tasks; secondary and danger variants for other actions.

rails.example:
<%= pb_rails("button", props: { variant: "primary" }) do %>
  Submit
<% end %>

button_toolbar.name: ButtonToolbar
button_toolbar.description: This component should primarily hold the most commonly used buttons.

rails.example:
<%= pb_rails("button_toolbar", props: { orientation: "horizontal", variant: "primary" }) do %>
  <Button text="Create" />
<Button text="Edit" />
<Button text="Delete" />
<% end %>

caption.name: Caption
caption.description: Supplementary text beside inputs or blocks; use large caption when the note spans more content.

react.example:
<Caption size="md">
  Figure 1 · Quarterly revenue by region
</Caption>

rails.example:
<%= pb_rails("caption", props: { size: "md" }) do %>
  Figure 1 · Quarterly revenue by region
<% end %>

card.name: Card
card.description: Content container with optional header, body sections, and various styling options.

rails.example:
<%= pb_rails("card", props: {  }) do %>
  Card content
<% end %>

checkbox.name: Checkbox
checkbox.description: Checkbox is used for a list of selections that are meant to have one or more options checked.

react.example: <Checkbox text="Subscribe to product updates" name="subscribe" value="yes" />

rails.example: <%= pb_rails("checkbox", props: { text: "Subscribe to product updates", name: "subscribe", value: "yes" }) %>

circle_icon_button.name: CircleIconButton
circle_icon_button.description: Round icon-only button; the icon must clearly show the action because there is no label.

rails.example: <%= pb_rails("circle_icon_button", props: { icon: "plus", variant: "primary" }) %>

collapsible.name: Collapsible
collapsible.description: Collapsible content that can be expanded or collapsed.

rails.example:
<%= pb_rails("collapsible", props: {  }) do %>
  Expandable content goes here.
<% end %>

contact.name: Contact
contact.description: Use to display customer's or user's contact information.

rails.example: <%= pb_rails("contact", props: { contact_type: "email", contact_value: "anna.black@example.com" }) %>

copy_button.name: CopyButton
copy_button.description: Button that copies text to clipboard with visual feedback.

rails.example: <%= pb_rails("copy_button", props: { tooltip_text: "Copied!", value: "Boo from Ghost Crew!" }) %>

currency.name: Currency
currency.description: Formats money for dashboards and summaries. Pair with labels so amounts stay clear.

rails.example: <%= pb_rails("currency", props: { amount: "2000" }) %>

dashboard_value.name: DashboardValue
dashboard_value.description: Large dashboard number for quick metrics. Use Currency when the value is money.

rails.example: <%= pb_rails("dashboard_value", props: { stat_label: "Monthly recurring revenue", stat_value: {"value":"1,428","unit":"appts"}, stat_change: {"change":"decrease","value":"26.1"} }) %>

date.name: Date
date.description: Use to display the date. Year will not display by default if it is the current year.

rails.example: <%= pb_rails("date", props: { value: "2026-04-09" }) %>

date_picker.name: DatePicker
date_picker.description: Calendar date field powered by flatpickr; props cover common cases without custom JS.

react.example: <DatePicker name="event_date" pickerId="playground-date-picker" label="Event date" placeholder="Select date" />

rails.example: <%= pb_rails("date_picker", props: { name: "event_date", picker_id: "playground-date-picker", label: "Event date", placeholder: "Select date" }) %>

date_range_inline.name: DateRangeInline
date_range_inline.description: Use to display a date range. Year will not show by default if it is the current year.

rails.example: <%= pb_rails("date_range_inline", props: { start_date: "2013-06-18", end_date: "2015-03-20" }) %>

date_range_stacked.name: DateRangeStacked
date_range_stacked.description: Displays a date range in a vertical stacked format.

rails.example: <%= pb_rails("date_range_stacked", props: { start_date: "2019-06-18", end_date: "2020-03-20" }) %>

date_stacked.name: DateStacked
date_stacked.description: Displays the date stacked with the month and day. Default behavior does not show the current year.

rails.example: <%= pb_rails("date_stacked", props: { date: "2026-04-09T12:00:00.000Z" }) %>

date_time.name: DateTime
date_time.description: Combined date and time. Respects time zones; defaults to America/New_York when not set.

rails.example: <%= pb_rails("date_time", props: { datetime: "2026-04-09T15:30:00.000Z" }) %>

date_time_stacked.name: DateTimeStacked
date_time_stacked.description: Displays date and time in a vertical stacked format.

rails.example: <%= pb_rails("date_time_stacked", props: { datetime: "2026-04-09T15:30:00.000Z" }) %>

date_year_stacked.name: DateYearStacked
date_year_stacked.description: This component is a simple option for displaying dates in a month, day, and year format.

rails.example: <%= pb_rails("date_year_stacked", props: { date: "2026-04-09" }) %>

detail.name: Detail
detail.description: Used for tables or designs with large amounts of data or text.

rails.example:
<%= pb_rails("detail", props: {  }) do %>
  I am a detail kit
<% end %>

dialog.name: Dialog
dialog.description: Modal for confirmations, forms, or focus. Supports alert modals for various statuses.

react.example:
<Dialog size="md" title="Header Title is the Title Prop" text="Hello Body Text, Nice to meet ya." cancelButton="Cancel Button" confirmButton="Okay">
  Custom dialog content goes here when you are not using the title and text props.
</Dialog>

rails.example:
<%= pb_rails("dialog", props: { size: "md", title: "Header Title is the Title Prop", text: "Hello Body Text, Nice to meet ya.", cancel_button: "Cancel Button", confirm_button: "Okay" }) do %>
  Custom dialog content goes here when you are not using the title and text props.
<% end %>

distribution_bar.name: DistributionBar
distribution_bar.description: Part-to-whole comparison like a pie chart. Default mode stresses share without raw numbers.

rails.example: <%= pb_rails("distribution_bar", props: { widths: [1,2,3,4,5,3,3,7] }) %>

draggable.name: Draggable
draggable.description: Drag and drop functionality for reordering items.

rails.example: <%= pb_rails("draggable", props: { drop_zone: {"type":"ghost","color":"neutral","direction":"vertical"} }) %>

dropdown.name: Dropdown
dropdown.description: Customizable dropdown menu with trigger element and various option configurations.

rails.example: <%= pb_rails("dropdown", props: { variant: "default", placeholder: "Select a country" }) %>

empty_state.name: EmptyState
empty_state.description: Empty state placeholder for when no content is available.

react.example: <EmptyState description="Body text goes into detail with possible steps for user to take" header="Title Explains" image="default" />

rails.example: <%= pb_rails("empty_state", props: { description: "Body text goes into detail with possible steps for user to take", header: "Title Explains", image: "default" }) %>

file_upload.name: FileUpload
file_upload.description: Allows users to upload files via drag-and-drop or file browser.

rails.example: <%= pb_rails("file_upload", props: {  }) %>

filter.name: Filter
filter.description: Search and filter UI. See production /dev_docs/search for real integration examples.

react.example: <Filter filters={{"Full Name":"John Wick"}} minWidth="360px" onSortChange="() => {}" results={546} sortOptions={{"popularity":"Popularity","manager_title":"Manager's Title","manager_name":"Manager's Name"}} sortValue={[{"name":"popularity","dir":"desc"}]} />

rails.example: <%= pb_rails("filter", props: { filters: {"Full Name":"John Wick"}, min_width: "360px", on_sort_change: "() => {}", results: 546, sort_options: {"popularity":"Popularity","manager_title":"Manager's Title","manager_name":"Manager's Name"}, sort_value: [{"name":"popularity","dir":"desc"}] }) %>

fixed_confirmation_toast.name: FixedConfirmationToast
fixed_confirmation_toast.description: Fixed alerts: success after completion, error when blocked, neutral for informational context.

rails.example: <%= pb_rails("fixed_confirmation_toast", props: { status: "success", text: "Items Successfully Moved" }) %>

flex.name: Flex
flex.description: Flexbox layout helper for responsive rows, columns, spacing, and alignment in UIs.

react.example:
<Flex horizontal="left" justify="none" orientation="row" vertical="top">
  <Caption text="A" />
<Caption text="B" />
<Caption text="C" />
</Flex>

rails.example:
<%= pb_rails("flex", props: { horizontal: "left", justify: "none", orientation: "row", vertical: "top" }) do %>
  <Caption text="A" />
<Caption text="B" />
<Caption text="C" />
<% end %>

form.name: Form
form.description: The Form component provides consumers with a convenient, consistently styled <form> wrapper.

rails.example: <%= pb_rails("form", props: { text: "Example" }) %>

form_group.name: FormGroup
form_group.description: Groups related form fields together with optional labels.

react.example:
<FormGroup>
  <TextInput
    id="first-name"
    label="First Name"
    name="firstName"
    onChange={handleFieldChange}
    placeholder="Enter first name"
    value={formFields.firstName}
/>
<TextInput
    id="middle-initial"
    label="Middle Initial"
    name="middleInitial"
    onChange={handleFieldChange}
    placeholder="Enter middle initial"
    value={formFields.middleInitial}
/>
<TextInput
    id="last-name"
    label="Last Name"
    name="lastName"
    onChange={handleFieldChange}
    placeholder="Enter last name"
    value={formFields.lastName}
/>
</FormGroup>

rails.example:
<%= pb_rails("form_group", props: {  }) do %>
  <TextInput
    id="first-name"
    label="First Name"
    name="firstName"
    onChange={handleFieldChange}
    placeholder="Enter first name"
    value={formFields.firstName}
/>
<TextInput
    id="middle-initial"
    label="Middle Initial"
    name="middleInitial"
    onChange={handleFieldChange}
    placeholder="Enter middle initial"
    value={formFields.middleInitial}
/>
<TextInput
    id="last-name"
    label="Last Name"
    name="lastName"
    onChange={handleFieldChange}
    placeholder="Enter last name"
    value={formFields.lastName}
/>
<% end %>

form_pill.name: FormPill
form_pill.description: Pill-shaped form elements for tags, selections, or filters.

react.example: <FormPill text="this is a tag" name="" icon="" />

rails.example: <%= pb_rails("form_pill", props: { text: "this is a tag", name: "", icon: "" }) %>

react.example:
<FullScreen contentPadding="lg" escToExit headerText="Enrollment Review" headerTextStyling="title_4" stickyHeader trigger="({ onClick, isOpen }) => (
  <Button
    marginBottom="md"
    onClick={onClick}
  >
    {isOpen ? "Exit Fullscreen" : "Enter Fullscreen"}
  </Button>
)">
  <Card padding="md">
  <Title size={4} text="Enrollment Review" />
  <Body marginTop="xs" text="Open fullscreen to review a focused workspace with enough content to test header behavior and padding." />
</Card>
</FullScreen>

rails.example:
<%= pb_rails("full_screen", props: { content_padding: "lg", esc_to_exit: true, header_text: "Enrollment Review", header_text_styling: "title_4", sticky_header: true, trigger: "({ onClick, isOpen }) => (
  <Button
    marginBottom="md"
    onClick={onClick}
  >
    {isOpen ? "Exit Fullscreen" : "Enter Fullscreen"}
  </Button>
)" }) do %>
  <Card padding="md">
  <Title size={4} text="Enrollment Review" />
  <Body marginTop="xs" text="Open fullscreen to review a focused workspace with enough content to test header behavior and padding." />
</Card>
<% end %>

hashtag.name: Hashtag
hashtag.description: Hashtag is used to display home, project and other forms of IDs. They can be used as a link.

rails.example: <%= pb_rails("hashtag", props: { text: "470297", type: "project", url: "https://google.com" }) %>

highlight.name: Highlight
highlight.description: Highlight is used to pick out or emphasize content.

react.example: <Highlight text="Use Highlight to call attention to important words in a sentence." highlightedText={["Highlight","important"]} />

rails.example: <%= pb_rails("highlight", props: { text: "Use Highlight to call attention to important words in a sentence.", highlighted_text: ["Highlight","important"] }) %>

home_address_street.name: HomeAddressStreet
home_address_street.description: Street address with unit, city, state, ZIP, and optional project hashtag linking to work.

react.example: <HomeAddressStreet address="70 Prospect Ave" addressCont="Apt M18" city="West Chester" state="PA" zipcode="19382" territory="PHL" houseStyle="Colonial" homeId="8250263" homeUrl="https://powerhrg.com/" emphasis="street" />

rails.example: <%= pb_rails("home_address_street", props: { address: "70 Prospect Ave", address_cont: "Apt M18", city: "West Chester", state: "PA", zipcode: "19382", territory: "PHL", house_style: "Colonial", home_id: "8250263", home_url: "https://powerhrg.com/", emphasis: "street" }) %>

icon.name: Icon
icon.description: Graphic symbol for an object, action, or status; add nearby text if meaning could be vague.

rails.example: <%= pb_rails("icon", props: { icon: "user", fixed_width: true }) %>

icon_button.name: IconButton
icon_button.description: Buttons are used primarily for actions, such as “Save” and “Cancel”. Link Buttons are used for less important or less commonly used actions, such as “view shipping settings”.

rails.example: <%= pb_rails("icon_button", props: { icon: "bars", size: "2x", variant: "default" }) %>

icon_circle.name: IconCircle
icon_circle.description: Icon centered in a circle for emphasis, touch targets, or consistent visual weight.

rails.example: <%= pb_rails("icon_circle", props: { icon: "rocket", size: "md", variant: "default" }) %>

icon_stat_value.name: IconStatValue
icon_stat_value.description: Displays a statistic value with an associated icon.

react.example: <IconStatValue icon="chart-line" value={1428} unit="hrs" text="Avg. session" orientation="horizontal" size="md" variant="default" />

rails.example: <%= pb_rails("icon_stat_value", props: { icon: "chart-line", value: 1428, unit: "hrs", text: "Avg. session", orientation: "horizontal", size: "md", variant: "default" }) %>

icon_value.name: IconValue
icon_value.description: Icon paired with a value—often a number—for compact KPIs, stats, or dense summaries.

rails.example: <%= pb_rails("icon_value", props: { icon: "heart", text: "93", align: "left" }) %>
<%= pb_rails("image", props: { url: "https://unsplash.it/500/400/?image=634", alt: "Misty forest", size: "md", transition: "fade" }) %>

label_pill.name: LabelPill
label_pill.description: This component combines the Caption and Pill components with all of their variants.

rails.example: <%= pb_rails("label_pill", props: { label: "Service Needed", pill_value: "76", variant: "neutral" }) %>

label_value.name: LabelValue
label_value.description: This component can be very versatile when used to display text data.

rails.example: <%= pb_rails("label_value", props: { label: "Role", value: "Administrator, Moderator", variant: "default" }) %>

layout.name: Layout
layout.description: Layouts used for positioning content inside of pages, cards, or containers.

react.example:

  <Layout.Side>
  Side
</Layout.Side>
<Layout.Body>
  Body
</Layout.Body>
</Layout>

rails.example:
<%= pb_rails("layout", props: { layout: "sidebar", position: "left", collapse: "md", size: "md", variant: "light" }) do %>
  <Layout.Side>

<Layout.Body>
  Body
</Layout.Body>

legend.name: Legend
legend.description: A key used to compare the variables and their value in any given graph.

rails.example: <%= pb_rails("legend", props: { text: "Revenue", color: "data_1" }) %>

link.name: Link
link.description: Text link for navigation to other pages or sections.

rails.example:
<%= pb_rails("link", props: { href: "#link-example", text: "Link text" }) do %>
  Link text
<% end %>

list.name: List
list.description: Lists display a vertical set of related content.

rails.example:
<%= pb_rails("list", props: {  }) do %>
  <ListItem>Item 1</ListItem>
<ListItem>Item 2</ListItem>
<ListItem>Item 3</ListItem>
<% end %>

loading_inline.name: LoadingInline
loading_inline.description: Inline spinner while content loads or a background request is still processing.

rails.example: <%= pb_rails("loading_inline", props: { align: "left" }) %>

map.name: Map
map.description: This component provides a wrapping class to place around the MapLibre library.

rails.example: <%= pb_rails("map", props: { zoom_btns: true, zoom_in_click: "() => handleZoomIn(mapInstance)", zoom_out_click: "() => handleZoomOut(mapInstance)" }) %>

externalDependencies.note: Map wraps MapLibre. The host app must already have maplibre-gl (and any required CSS) installed. Agents must not install packages — tell the user if they are missing.

message.name: Message
message.description: Conversation-style block with optional avatar, status, caption, body, and timestamp.

multi_level_select.description: The MultiLevelSelect component renders a multi leveled select dropdown based on data from the User.

react.example: <MultiLevelSelect variant="multi" label="Departments" placeholder="Search teams..." inputDisplay="pills" onSelect="(selectedNodes) => console.log('Selected Items', selectedNodes)" />

multiple_users.name: MultipleUsers

pb_bar_graph.name: PbBarGraph
pb_bar_graph.description: Bar graphs are used to compare data. Bar graphs are not typically used to show percentages.

react.example: <PbBarGraph options={{"series":[{"name":"Installation","data":[1475,200,3000,654,656]},{"name":"Manufacturing","data":[4434,524,2320,440,500]},{"name":"Sales & Distribution","data":[3387,743,1344,434,440]},{"name":"Project Development","data":[3227,878,999,780,1000]},{"name":"Other","data":[1111,677,3245,500,200]}],"title":{"text":"Solar Employment Growth by Sector, 2010-2016"},"subtitle":{"text":"Source: thesolarfoundation.com"},"xAxis":{"categories":["Jan","Feb","Mar","Apr","May"]},"yAxis":{"title":{"text":"Number of Employees"}}}} />

pb_line_graph.description: Line graph for displaying data trends over time.

react.example: <PbLineGraph options={{"series":[{"name":"Installation","data":[43934,52503,57177,69658,97031,119931,137133,154175]},{"name":"Manufacturing","data":[24916,24064,29742,29851,32490,30282,38121,40434]},{"name":"Sales & Distribution","data":[11744,17722,16005,19771,20185,24377,32147,39387]},{"name":"Project Development","data":[null,null,7988,12169,15112,22452,34400,34227]},{"name":"Other","data":[12908,5948,8105,11248,8989,11816,18274,18111]}],"title":{"text":"Solar Employment Growth by Sector, 2010-2016"},"subtitle":{"text":"Source: thesolarfoundation.com"},"xAxis":{"categories":["Jan","Feb","Mar","Apr","May","Jun","Jul","Aug"]},"yAxis":{"title":{"text":"Number of Employees"}}}} />

rails.example: <%= pb_rails("pb_line_graph", props: { options: {"series":[{"name":"Installation","data":[43934,52503,57177,69658,97031,119931,137133,154175]},{"name":"Manufacturing","data":[24916,24064,29742,29851,32490,30282,38121,40434]},{"name":"Sales & Distribution","data":[11744,17722,16005,19771,20185,24377,32147,39387]},{"name":"Project Development","data":[null,null,7988,12169,15112,22452,34400,34227]},{"name":"Other","data":[12908,5948,8105,11248,8989,11816,18274,18111]}],"title":{"text":"Solar Employment Growth by Sector, 2010-2016"},"subtitle":{"text":"Source: thesolarfoundation.com"},"xAxis":{"categories":["Jan","Feb","Mar","Apr","May","Jun","Jul","Aug"]},"yAxis":{"title":{"text":"Number of Employees"}}} }) %>

externalDependencies.note: This kit wraps Highcharts and does not ship it. The host app must already have these packages installed before using the kit. Agents must not install packages — tell the user if they are missing.

person.name: Person
person.description: This component is broken down into a first name last name format with normal and bold weighted text.

rails.example: <%= pb_rails("person", props: { first_name: "Kyle", last_name: "Fadigan" }) %>

person_contact.name: PersonContact
person_contact.description: This component can be used to display a person contact information.

rails.example: <%= pb_rails("person_contact", props: { first_name: "Pauline", last_name: "Smith", contacts: [{"contactType":"email","contactValue":"email@example.com"},{"contactValue":"5555555555"},{"contactType":"work","contactValue":"3245627482"}] }) %>

phone_number_input.name: PhoneNumberInput
phone_number_input.description: International phone number input with country code selection and formatting.

rails.example: <%= pb_rails("phone_number_input", props: { id: "phone-number-default", initial_country: "us", label: "Phone Number", name: "phone_number" }) %>

pill.name: Pill
pill.description: A pill uses both a keyword and a specific color to categorize an item.

rails.example: <%= pb_rails("pill", props: { text: "neutral", variant: "neutral", text_transform: "lowercase" }) %>

popover.name: Popover
popover.description: Anchored panel for short content, mini forms, or menus. Click the trigger to toggle it open.

react.example:
<Popover closeOnClick="outside" placement="top">
  I'm a popover. I can show content of any size.
</Popover>

rails.example:
<%= pb_rails("popover", props: { close_on_click: "outside", placement: "top" }) do %>
  I'm a popover. I can show content of any size.
<% end %>

progress_pills.name: ProgressPills
progress_pills.description: Step chips along a sequence—shows completed, current, and upcoming stages over time.

rails.example: <%= pb_rails("progress_pills", props: { steps: 4, active: 1, title: "Checkout", value: "Shipping" }) %>

progress_simple.name: ProgressSimple
progress_simple.description: Linear progress for an operation; add labels or percentages so progress is obvious.

rails.example: <%= pb_rails("progress_simple", props: { percent: "0" }) %>

progress_step.name: ProgressStep
progress_step.description: Wizard steps marked completed, active, or inactive for multi-phase flows.

rails.example:
<%= pb_rails("progress_step", props: {  }) do %>
  <ProgressStepItem status="complete">Step 1</ProgressStepItem>
<ProgressStepItem status="active">Step 2</ProgressStepItem>
<ProgressStepItem status="inactive">Step 3</ProgressStepItem>
<% end %>

radio.name: Radio
radio.description: Radio is a control that allows the user to only choose one predefined option.

react.example:
<Radio label="Standard shipping" name="shipping_method" value="standard" text="Standard shipping">
  <Title text="Custom radio content" />
</Radio>

rails.example:
<%= pb_rails("radio", props: { label: "Standard shipping", name: "shipping_method", value: "standard", text: "Standard shipping" }) do %>
  <Title text="Custom radio content" />
<% end %>

rich_text_editor.name: RichTextEditor
rich_text_editor.description: Full-featured text editor with formatting options.

rails.example: <%= pb_rails("rich_text_editor", props: { advanced_editor_toolbar: true, label: "Description", name: "description" }) %>

externalDependencies.note: Default React editor uses Trix (pass TrixEditor from react-trix). Advanced editor uses TipTap. The host app must already have the needed packages installed. Agents must not install packages — tell the user if they are missing. Rails advanced TipTap may load via the kit’s esm.sh script.

section_separator.name: SectionSeparator
section_separator.description: A divider line that visually separates and organizes content into distinct sections.

rails.example: <%= pb_rails("section_separator", props: { orientation: "horizontal", line_style: "solid", color: "default", variant: "card" }) %>

select.name: Select
select.description: Dropdown where the user picks one option from a list, styled like other form fields.

rails.example: <%= pb_rails("select", props: { label: "Country", name: "country", value: "us", options: [{"value":"us","text":"United States"},{"value":"ca","text":"Canada"},{"value":"uk","text":"United Kingdom"},{"value":"au","text":"Australia"}] }) %>

selectable_card.name: SelectableCard
selectable_card.description: Selectable card with clear selected and unselected visuals; common for plans or tiers.

react.example:
<SelectableCard checked={false} inputId="plan_standard" name="selectable_card_demo" text="Standard plan" value="standard" multi variant="default">
  <Title size={4} text="Pro plan" />
<Body color="light" text="Includes advanced reporting." />
</SelectableCard>

rails.example:
<%= pb_rails("selectable_card", props: { checked: false, input_id: "plan_standard", name: "selectable_card_demo", text: "Standard plan", value: "standard", multi: true, variant: "default" }) do %>
  <Title size={4} text="Pro plan" />
<Body color="light" text="Includes advanced reporting." />
<% end %>

selectable_card_icon.name: SelectableCardIcon
selectable_card_icon.description: Selectable card variant with icon display for visual selection options.

react.example: <SelectableCardIcon bodyText="Export" icon="chart-line" inputId="report_quarterly" name="report_type" titleText="Quarterly Report" value="quarterly" />

rails.example: <%= pb_rails("selectable_card_icon", props: { body_text: "Export", icon: "chart-line", input_id: "report_quarterly", name: "report_type", title_text: "Quarterly Report", value: "quarterly" }) %>

selectable_icon.name: SelectableIcon
selectable_icon.description: Icon-based selection input for compact visual choices.

react.example: <SelectableIcon icon="user" text="Assignee" name="assignee" inputId="assignee_1" value="user1" checked={false} multi inputs="enabled" />

rails.example: <%= pb_rails("selectable_icon", props: { icon: "user", text: "Assignee", name: "assignee", input_id: "assignee_1", value: "user1", checked: false, multi: true, inputs: "enabled" }) %>

selectable_list.name: SelectableList
selectable_list.description: List of items that can be selected, supporting single or multiple selection.

react.example:
<SelectableList variant="checkbox" enableDrag={false}>
  <SelectableList.Item label="Mild" name="spice" value="mild" />
<SelectableList.Item checked label="Medium" name="spice" value="medium" />
<SelectableList.Item label="Hot" name="spice" value="hot" />
</SelectableList>

rails.example:
<%= pb_rails("selectable_list", props: { variant: "checkbox", enable_drag: false }) do %>
  <SelectableList.Item label="Mild" name="spice" value="mild" />
<SelectableList.Item checked label="Medium" name="spice" value="medium" />
<SelectableList.Item label="Hot" name="spice" value="hot" />
<% end %>

skeleton_loading.name: SkeletonLoading
skeleton_loading.description: Placeholder loading state that mimics the shape of content.

rails.example: <%= pb_rails("skeleton_loading", props: { height: "16px", width: "100%" }) %>

source.name: Source
source.description: Shows where a record or lead came from; flexible for other attribution labels too.

rails.example: <%= pb_rails("source", props: { source: "Website lead", type: "inbound" }) %>

star_rating.name: StarRating
star_rating.description: Star rating for opinions or scores; pair with reviews or labels for real meaning.

rails.example: <%= pb_rails("star_rating", props: { rating: 4, denominator: 5, variant: "display" }) %>

stat_change.name: StatChange
stat_change.description: Displays the increase, decrease, or neutral change in data.

rails.example: <%= pb_rails("stat_change", props: { change: "increase", value: "15" }) %>

stat_value.name: StatValue
stat_value.description: Prominent numeric stat for dashboards; optional label explains what the figure means.

rails.example: <%= pb_rails("stat_value", props: { value: 1428, unit: "hrs" }) %>

table.name: Table
table.description: Structured rows and columns of data, often with sorting, filtering, and pagination.

rails.example:
<%= pb_rails("table", props: { size: "sm", responsive: "collapse" }) do %>
  <Table.Head>
  <Table.Row>
    <Table.Header text="Territory ID" />
    <Table.Header text="Name" />
    <Table.Header text="Status" />
    <Table.Header text="Start Date" textAlign="right" />
  </Table.Row>
</Table.Head>
<Table.Body>
  <Table.Row>
    <Table.Cell text="1001" numberSpacing="tabular" />
    <Table.Cell text="Ada Lovelace" />
    <Table.Cell text="Active" />
    <Table.Cell text="Apr 9, 2026" textAlign="right" />
  </Table.Row>
  <Table.Row>
    <Table.Cell text="1002" numberSpacing="tabular" />
    <Table.Cell text="Grace Hopper" />
    <Table.Cell text="Pending" />
    <Table.Cell text="Apr 10, 2026" textAlign="right" />
  </Table.Row>
  <Table.Row>
    <Table.Cell text="1003" numberSpacing="tabular" />
    <Table.Cell text="Katherine Johnson" />
    <Table.Cell text="Active" />
    <Table.Cell text="Apr 11, 2026" textAlign="right" />
  </Table.Row>
</Table.Body>
<% end %>

text_input.name: TextInput
text_input.description: Area where user can enter small amount of text. Commonly used in forms.

rails.example: <%= pb_rails("text_input", props: { label: "Email", name: "email", placeholder: "you@example.com", value: "" }) %>

textarea.name: Textarea
textarea.description: Area where user can enter larger amounts of text. Commonly used in forms.

react.example: <Textarea label="Description" name="description" placeholder="Tell us more about your project…" value="" />

rails.example: <%= pb_rails("textarea", props: { label: "Description", name: "description", placeholder: "Tell us more about your project…", value: "" }) %>

time.name: Time
time.description: Displays a time of day with optional timezone and icon, in large or compact layouts.

time_picker.name: TimePicker
time_picker.description: A time picker component that allows users to select a time independently of the date.

rails.example: <%= pb_rails("time_picker", props: { label: "Start time", name: "start_time", default_time: "3:30 PM" }) %>

time_range_inline.name: TimeRangeInline
time_range_inline.description: Displays a time range in an inline format.

rails.example: <%= pb_rails("time_range_inline", props: { start_time: "2026-04-09T15:30:00.000Z", end_time: "2026-04-09T17:00:00.000Z" }) %>

time_stacked.name: TimeStacked
time_stacked.description: Displays time in a vertical stacked format.

rails.example: <%= pb_rails("time_stacked", props: { time: 1775748600000 }) %>

timeline.name: Timeline
timeline.description: A timeline with solid or dotted connectors to show sequences, phases, or gaps in time.

react.example:
<Timeline>
  <Timeline.Item icon="file-alt">Request received</Timeline.Item>
<Timeline.Item icon="user" lineStyle="dotted">Assigned to reviewer</Timeline.Item>
<Timeline.Item icon="check">Approved</Timeline.Item>
</Timeline>

rails.example:
<%= pb_rails("timeline", props: {  }) do %>
  <Timeline.Item icon="file-alt">Request received</Timeline.Item>
<Timeline.Item icon="user" lineStyle="dotted">Assigned to reviewer</Timeline.Item>
<Timeline.Item icon="check">Approved</Timeline.Item>
<% end %>

timestamp.name: Timestamp
timestamp.description: Low profile component for displaying time; elapsed, current, future, or otherwise.

rails.example: <%= pb_rails("timestamp", props: { timestamp: "2026-04-09T15:30:00.000Z", text: "Alex Chen" }) %>

title.name: Title
title.description: Heading levels Title 1-4; keep semantic order and do not skip levels on a page.

rails.example:
<%= pb_rails("title", props: { size: 3, tag: "h3", text: "Section heading" }) do %>
  Title
<% end %>

title_count.name: TitleCount
title_count.description: Title with a related count, in default or larger dashboard-friendly sizing.

rails.example: <%= pb_rails("title_count", props: { title: "Active users", count: 1428, align: "left", size: "sm" }) %>

title_detail.name: TitleDetail
title_detail.description: This component can be used in many versatile ways. It's made up of a Title 4 and light Body component.

react.example: <TitleDetail title="Revenue" detail="$2,000 MRR · 15% vs last month" align="left" />

rails.example: <%= pb_rails("title_detail", props: { title: "Revenue", detail: "$2,000 MRR · 15% vs last month", align: "left" }) %>

toggle.name: Toggle
toggle.description: On/off switch for settings, feature flags, or any binary choice in a form.

rails.example: <%= pb_rails("toggle", props: { name: "marketing_emails", value: "opt_in" }) %>

tooltip.name: Tooltip
tooltip.description: Small overlay providing contextual information on hover or focus.

react.example:
<Tooltip placement="top" text="Tooltip on top">
  Hover me
</Tooltip>

rails.example:
<%= pb_rails("tooltip", props: { placement: "top", text: "Tooltip on top" }) do %>
  Hover me
<% end %>

typeahead.name: Typeahead
typeahead.description: Autocomplete options that narrow as users type, cutting errors and extra typing.

rails.example: <%= pb_rails("typeahead", props: { label: "Colors", name: "color", options: [{"label":"Orange","value":"#FFA500"},{"label":"Red","value":"#FF0000"},{"label":"Green","value":"#00FF00"},{"label":"Blue","value":"#0000FF"}] }) %>

user.name: User
user.description: Avatar with name, title, territory, and optional extras—the standard rich user row.

react.example: <User name="Anna Black" title="Engineer" subtitle="Product team" avatar avatarUrl="https://randomuser.me/api/portraits/women/44.jpg" size="md" orientation="horizontal" />

rails.example: <%= pb_rails("user", props: { name: "Anna Black", title: "Engineer", subtitle: "Product team", avatar: true, avatar_url: "https://randomuser.me/api/portraits/women/44.jpg", size: "md", orientation: "horizontal" }) %>

user_badge.name: UserBadge
user_badge.description: Small badge on an avatar for programs or achievements so standout users read quickly.

rails.example: <%= pb_rails("user_badge", props: { badge: "million-dollar", size: "md" }) %>

weekday_stacked.name: WeekdayStacked
weekday_stacked.description: Displays day of week and date in a stacked format.

rails.example: <%= pb_rails("weekday_stacked", props: { date: "2026-04-09T12:00:00.000Z" }) %>
